maria: Quick sync — canary showing classifier jitter. Adaptive seq-len classifier is oscillating around the 32-40 token range and ~2.7% of requests briefly route to long-path, causing KV cache misses and latency spikes. Anyone seen similar?

raj: Can you paste the classifier config and the window stats?

maria: Current config (simple tree + median smoothing):
```json
{"classifier": "slen-tree", "thresholds": [16, 64], "smoothing": {"method": "median", "window": 5}}
```
Observed: when client sequences hover 30-36 tokens we flip paths frequently. KV eviction spike correlates with flips.

kai: Profiling snapshot: when seq in [30,36] prefill->decode handoff shows L2 miss spike and scheduler stalls. Quick counters: prefill L2_MISS +18k, decode L2_MISS +3k. KV cache eviction rate jumps x4 at boundaries.

jules: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) switch to EWMA smoothing instead of median to reduce flip frequency; 2) move the short->long boundary upward to 40 for canary and see effect. EWMA pseudo: `ewma_t = alpha * len_t + (1-alpha) * ewma_{t-1}`; try alpha=0.3.

raj: Also add a transition metric: per-session transition_count over 1m window. If transitions > 2, bias classifier toward long-path to avoid thrash. Instrumentation will help quantify impact.

deploy-bot: deploy: scheduling canary "slen-classifier/ewma-alpha0.3" -> rollout 10% at 2026-03-17T15:23:00Z :rocket:

maria: Thanks — I'll watch latency, KV hit-rate, and cost dashboards. If anyone grabs traces/logs, please ping me. Adding :eyes: for now.
